english: Under what circumstances does 5 follow from 2?
topic: Hilbert considers how six previously listed properties of invariants imply one another, then begins stating a general theorem about systems of rational functions and integral rational functions in variables x_1,...,x_n that he wants to prove.

triage.modern_statement: The note is only a cross-reference: 'property 5' and 'property 2' point to a list of six properties of invariants that is not quoted here, so what they say cannot be confirmed. A tentative reading comes from the next part of the page, where Hilbert starts a general theorem about systems of rational functions and integral rational (polynomial) functions in x_1,...,x_n. Read that way, the question may be: if a system of invariants is finitely generated as rational functions (a subfield K of k(x_1,...,x_n)), when does it follow that the integral rational invariants, the ring K ∩ k[x_1,...,x_n], are also finitely generated? Put differently, when does finite generation of the field of rational invariants give finite generation of the ring of polynomial invariants? This is the question behind Hilbert's 14th problem (1900). The identification is a guess, not something the page itself establishes.
triage.answered_by: This only applies if the tentative reading is right. Hilbert's 14th problem asks whether K ∩ k[x_1,...,x_n] is always finitely generated over k. Zariski gave positive results in 1954 (transcendence degree ≤ 2). Nagata gave the first counterexamples in 1958–59, including a ring of invariants of a linear group action, which settled the general question negatively. Later counterexamples include those of Rees, Roberts and others.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's fourteenth problem asks whether, for a subfield K of k(x_1..x_n) containing k, the intersection K ∩ k^[n] is finitely generated over k. Nagata presented the first counterexamples in 1958.
Hilbert conjectured that all such algebras are finitely generated; in 1959 Nagata found a counterexample, a ring of polynomial invariants of a linear algebraic group.
Related questions are still studied, e.g. whether the kernel of a locally nilpotent derivation of k^[n] is finitely generated, and Zariski's generalization.
